entities.summary: Gregory Chi-Chong Chow is a Chinese-American economist at Princeton University and Xiamen University. The Chow test, commonly used in econometrics to test for structural breaks, was invented by him. He has also been influential in the economic policy of China, including being an adviser for the Economic Planning and Development Council of the Executive Yuan in the Republic of China, and being an adviser for the Chinese State Commission for Restructuring the Economic System on economic reform.
